source.citation: Salt C, Morris PJ, German AJ, et al. Growth standard charts for monitoring bodyweight in dogs of different sizes. PLoS ONE 2017;12(9):e0182064.
source.correction: PLoS One 2024;19(11):e0314711 corrects only the Data Availability statement; method unchanged.

method.population: dogs confirmed lean (Normal body condition) at 2-3 years, with no recorded Thin/Heavy visit at any age (Policy C); all their 0.20-2.25y preventive/healthy, not-yet-neutered visits
method.ageBins: weekly 12-28 wk; 8- or 12-week bins across the 28-52 wk adolescent gap; 4-weekly 52-104 wk; bins with n<200 interpolated (isotonic), not observed
method.smoothing: monotone isotonic regression on median, capped at 1.0
method.normalization: per band, plateau = median ratio across observed 96-104 week visits; normalized = raw / plateau. Adult weight means the typical weight of healthy-weight dogs at 2 years; breed averages that include older, heavier dogs run higher.
